text:
Mikael Granlund is 34, on his sixth NHL team, and near a point a game: 29 in 25 games, with three assists against San Jose on Nov. 25. The Hockey News called him under the radar and on pace for triple digits.

Our numbers are the skeptics here. Anaheim gets only 41% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) when he's on the ice, worse than when he sits, yet the Ducks have scored 11.1 more goals than those chances deserve with him out there. That gap is padding his total, and on-ice luck like that fades. His points rate is well above our talent range for him, too. What he does well is real: he moves the puck, with 13 power-play points, and Evolving-Hockey had him driving play in the 90th percentile last season. With Leo Carlsson hurt, he'll get the minutes. Our numbers project about 81 points. Watch the five-on-five share; that's where this season either holds or slides.
headline: Granlund's points outrun what happens on ice
